title: The student who asked about om
hook: Satyakama asks what a life of om leads to; a, u, m hold waking, dream and deep sleep
carry: a, u, m: waking, dream, deep sleep
tomorrow: The teacher who answered with silence

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Mandukya Upanishad: turiya, the awareness under every state. After a hundred and one years, Indra learned the self is the knower behind every state.

Six seekers once came to a sage named Pippalada, firewood in hand. He told them: live here a year first, with discipline and faith. Then ask anything. One of them, Satyakama, asked what any chanting family might ask. Sir, if someone meditates on om all their life, to the very end, where does it lead? Pippalada said: om is Brahman, both the higher and the lower. Hold one part of it, and you go part of the way. Hold all three of its sounds together, and you reach the highest.
screen: `A YEAR BEFORE A QUESTION.` → `WHERE DOES OM LEAD?` → `ALL THREE SOUNDS TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Three sounds? The Mandukya spells them out. Verse eight: this self, as a syllable, is om. The quarters are the letters, and the letters are the quarters: a, u, m. In Sanskrit the o of om is a and u blended, which is why it's also written aum. Verse nine: waking is a, the first sound, the open mouth. Verse ten: dream is u, the rounding lips, in between, the way dream sits between waking and sleep. Verse eleven: deep sleep is m, the lips closing, where the sound gathers, the way waking and dream fold into sleep each night. The text backs each link with wordplay, a sound suggesting a meaning, the kind the Upanishads use often. So say it slowly: ah, oo, mmm. Back of the throat, to the lips, closed. One breath walks through a whole day and night. And the fourth? It has no letter. That's tomorrow. This is why om comes first in so many Hindu mantras: om namah shivaya, om namo narayanaya. Before you ask for anything, you name all of it: everything you're awake to, everything you dream, everything you rest in. Some families say a quiet om before a long drive or an exam for the same reason. Today, most days are lived in pieces: the morning rush, the scrolling half-dream, the crash at night. Om is the Hindu way of holding the whole day in one breath, and offering it.
screen: `THE LETTERS ARE THE QUARTERS.` · `A WAKING, U DREAM, M SLEEP.` · `SAY IT SLOWLY: AH, OO, MMM.` · `OM COMES FIRST.` · then, large: `A, U, M.`

segments.voice: If you're comfortable, chant om slowly three times, out loud or silently, feeling each sound in your mouth: on the ah, think waking; on the oo, dream; on the mmm, deep sleep. After the third, stay in the silence and add nothing. If chanting isn't your practice, simply breathe in three parts and rest after each out-breath.
The Mandukya Upanishad. Om, letter by letter: a is waking, u is dream, m is deep sleep. The fourth has no letter.
Your line: a, u, m: waking, dream, deep sleep. A whole day and night in one syllable. That's day two hundred fifty-eight.

screen: `DAY 258 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE TEACHER WHO ANSWERED WITH SILENCE.`

howItsDone: Hindu teachers who follow the Mandukya instruct students to chant om as three sounds, a-u-m, followed by silence, following the Mandukya's mapping of the letters to waking, dream and deep sleep.

chat.says: dad says om before EVERY prayer. also before starting the car, next to his dashboard hanuman 🙄 Sam asked why om always goes first
options: om holds everything: a is waking, u is dream, m is deep sleep. you name the whole of life before you ask for anything.

chat.meaning: The Mandukya maps om's three sounds onto waking, dream and deep sleep, and Pippalada taught that holding all of om leads to the highest. So Hindus put om first.

tie.story: Satyakama asked Pippalada where a life of chanting om leads, and learned that all three sounds together reach the highest.
tie.friend: Priya can tell Sam her dad's om names the whole of life, waking, dream and sleep, before he asks for anything.
tie.you: what would you want to hold whole before you begin?
